```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(kableExtra)
library(gtExtras)
library(gt)
library(formattable)

```

## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
read.csv("Massey_raw_data.csv") ->data
data

```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
data %>% 
  filter(grepl('Waste', Area)) ->data2
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.


```{r}
options(scipen=999)
data2 %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=Area, y=Quantity)) + geom_col(aes(fill= Area))

data2 %>% 
  select(Business, Area, Quantity) %>%
  filter(Quantity > 0) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Massey Univeristy KG waste sent to landfill as at December 31 2019"
  )

data2 %>%
  summarise(sum(Quantity))
```


```{r}
read.csv("data3.csv") ->data4
data4 %>% 
  filter(Quantity > 0) %>%
  select(Grouping, Quantity, Unit) %>%
  group_by(Grouping) %>%
  summarise(Quantity = sum(Quantity), Unit) %>%
  filter (Unit != 'dollars')->data5


unique(data5)->data5
data5

data5 %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=Grouping, y = Quantity)) + geom_col(aes(fill=Unit)) +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1))+ 
  labs(title = "Massey University, Quantity of emission generating 'waste' by type")

data5 %>%
  formattable

data5 %>%
  ungroup(Grouping) %>%
  select(Quantity) %>%
  summarise(sum(Quantity))
```
